purpose: Complete source roster of fifteen fixed Behenian stars with the explicitly listed stones and plants; no Voynich target was read or scored.

source.primary_title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book I, chapter XXXII
source.author: Henry Cornelius Agrippa
source.edition: 1651 English translation, institutional EEBO full text
source.corroborating_locator: Chapter XXXII, printed pp. 64-65, HTML lines 692-702
source.historical_context: BPHV describes a shorter Latin translation dated 1360, laid out similarly to a Tractatus de quindecim stellis, with fifteenth-century witnesses; it does not itself establish this exact 15-row plant wording.
source.source_limit: This is an early-modern English witness/reproduction, not proof that every entry is preserved unchanged from a medieval source.

herbs_exact: Suc-cory, whose leaves, and Flowers turn towards the North

stones_exact: such stones as are of the Colour of the black Onyx stone

cross_star_statement: The following paragraph explicitly says a plant or stone may receive conjoined influence from many stars; it separately names Mastick under the Heart of the Lyon and Mint under the Goat star.
scope_flags: Direct row incidence is kept separate from the later cross-star paragraph.
Old spellings and qualifiers are not modernized or merged: Perwinckle/Perwinkle, Suc-cory/Succory, Mandrake/the root of Mandrake.
Flowers and root are preserved as plant-part qualifiers; treating them as the same botanical identity is an optional later hypothesis, not an observation.
No modern identification of Diacedon, Matry-silva, Quadraginus, Penyroial, or other names is asserted.
